mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the Federal Funds rate above 4% in the month preceding the forecast period coincides with a short-term discount rate premium for equities, pushing 20-day S&P 500 forward returns negative.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS crosses above 4.0% in the month prior to the forecast month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically different from zero during tightening episodes (t-test p > 0.05); or FEDFUNDS does not exceed 4.0% in the preceding month.

mechanism_narrative: Persistent declines in CPIAUCSL (inflation) for three consecutive months signal disinflation, which reduces risk premia and drives positive 60-day S&P 500 forward returns.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL falls for three consecutive months
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not statistically positive during confirmed disinflation periods (t-test p > 0.05); or CPIAUCSL does not show three consecutive monthly declines.

mechanism_narrative: A sudden jump in PAYEMS (labor market strength) accompanied by a simultaneous drop in UNRATE (labor supply) creates a labor-market tightness signal that predicts positive 20-day S&P 500 returns.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases by at least 10% in one month while UNRATE falls by at least 0.2 percentage points
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically positive when both proxies move in opposite directions (Pearson correlation < 0.3); or the interaction effect is not significant in a two-variable regression.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in GDPC1 (real private consumption) above the prior quarter's average in the current quarter signals strong consumer demand, which is associated with positive 5-day S&P 500 forward returns.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 exceeds QoQ average by at least 3% in the current quarter
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are not positive when GDPC1 growth is below QoQ average (t-test p > 0.05); or the effect is not significant in a regression with lagged returns.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in INDPRO (industrial production) for two consecutive months indicates supply-side weakness, which tends to depress equity valuations and produce negative 20-day S&P 500 forward returns.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO falls for two consecutive months
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically negative during confirmed supply shocks (t-test p > 0.05); or INDPRO recovers in the next month without a reversal in returns.

mechanism_narrative: When FEDFUNDS remains below 2.5% for three consecutive months during a non-expansionary regime, it creates a persistent risk-off environment that is associated with negative 60-day S&P 500 forward returns.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS < 2.5% for three consecutive months and regime_hint is not 'expansionary'
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not consistently negative in such regimes (t-test p > 0.05); or FEDFUNDS crosses above 2.5% before returns recover.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in HOUST (housing starts) combined with a simultaneous decline in UNRATE signals a housing recovery coupled with tighter labor supply, which predicts positive 20-day S&P 500 returns.
candidate_trigger: HOUST increases by at least 5% in a month while UNRATE falls by at least 0.1 percentage points
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not positive when both proxies move in opposite directions (interaction p-value > 0.05); or the joint effect is not significant in a regression.

mechanism_narrative: When RSAFS (retail sales) falls for two consecutive months while UNRATE remains flat or rises, it indicates softening consumer demand without labor loosening, which tends to depress equities and drive negative 5-day S&P 500 forward returns.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS decreases for two consecutive months and UNRATE does not fall
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are not statistically negative when demand weakness is not confirmed by labor data (Pearson correlation < -0.2); or the interaction effect is not significant.
